brt-cavalry-emp-pikes.name: brt-cavalry-emp-pikes
brt-cavalry-emp-pikes.brief: Six fully mounted units; Grail Knights anchor the shock force. Four halberds cover two handguns and a cannon. Maneuver, engagement angle, target priority and disengagement compete; frontal grinding is the naive risk. Hypotheses, not a prescribed solution.

tze-caster-skv-screen.loadouts: Default recruitment upgrades, all equipped; recorded in starting ability fingerprint. Explicit mount where declared.
tze-caster-skv-screen.name: tze-caster-skv-screen
tze-caster-skv-screen.brief: Kairos and four escorts face ten Skaven units. Spell value, shared magic, screening, barrier recovery and flying-unit risk compete with artillery pressure. This is a compact caster test, not the later massive-swarm scenario. Hypotheses, not a prescribed solution.

brt-cavalry-emp-pegasus.name: brt-cavalry-emp-pegasus
brt-cavalry-emp-pegasus.brief: Six fully mounted units, with Grail Knights as the player anchor, face four halberds, two handguns, a cannon and a general on an Imperial Pegasus. The faster flying lord is an enemy anchor intended to pressure simple evasion. Interception, engagement angle, target priority and disengagement compete. AI pursuit is a hypothesis to verify, not a guaranteed script.
brt-cavalry-emp-pegasus.calibration_change: The pikes-only development screen lost with both trivial controls; Luna chose untouched evasion for a timeout win and was deliberately interrupted, with no gameplay outcome. Replace the enemy foot general with the verified speed 105 Pegasus mount (versus friendly 84/92) while retaining all other units and the 8000 cap. Original screen remains recorded.

brt-cavalry-emp-assault.name: brt-cavalry-emp-assault
brt-cavalry-emp-assault.brief: Six fully mounted units, anchored by Grail Knights, must assault an Empire defense of four halberds, two handguns, a cannon and a foot general. The attacker loses at the finite timer. Choice of approach, splitting the defense, engagement angles, target priority and disengagement compete; no tactic is prescribed to the controller.
brt-cavalry-emp-assault.calibration_change: Reverse the player role of the original six-versus-eight foot-general prototype. Defender evasion was legitimate but offered weak tactical pressure; this new task requires defeating the enemy within 1200 seconds. Roster, map, funds and stat modifier retain their corresponding original values. This is a separate development hypothesis, not a continuation of earlier performance results.

tze-caster-skv-assault.name: tze-caster-skv-assault
tze-caster-skv-assault.brief: Kairos and four escorts must assault a ten-unit Skaven army with expendable bodies, a warpfire team and a plagueclaw catapult. Spell selection, finite Winds of Magic, barrier recovery, flight and escort survival compete. The player loses at the 1200-second timer, so indefinite passive survival cannot meet the objective. These are design hypotheses, not prescribed tactics.
tze-caster-skv-assault.calibration_change: Separate attacker-role candidate preserving the five-versus-ten defender roster, default spellbook, funds and corresponding maps/modifiers. Sol demonstrated a ground cast, then chose defender timeout preservation in the development pilot. No gameplay result or performance ranking is inferred from that observation; this variant requires separate live setup and viability checks.

skv-swarm-dwf-line.name: skv-swarm-dwf-line
skv-swarm-dwf-line.brief: Twenty Skaven units, most of them cheap and quick to flee, must break nine Dwarf units holding a gun line with an Organ Gun before the 1200-second timer. A Warlord, a Warlock Engineer (the only caster), warpfire, poisoned wind, a Warp Lightning Cannon and a Doomwheel are the scarce damage. Spending slaves to screen and pin, timing the weapon teams, protecting the engineer and avoiding a cascade of routs compete; one all-in charge is the naive risk. Hypotheses, not a prescribed solution. Screened 2026-10-15: the lobby takes both rosters at 12000 and the AI holds its line.
skv-swarm-dwf-line.calibration_change: The first screen (bench-b10-screen-skv-swarm-20261015) stopped in the lobby: it offered no wh2_main_skv_cha_grey_seer_ruin_0 card. The Warlord, whose card worked in tze-caster-skv-screen, leads instead; the Warlock Engineer is the caster.

dwf-line-skv-swarm.name: dwf-line-skv-swarm
dwf-line-skv-swarm.brief: Seven Dwarf units must hold against twenty attacking Skaven units; the defender wins if it survives the 1200-second timer. Irondrakes and an Organ Gun are the only crowd-clearing anchors, with limited ammunition. Shaping the approach, anchoring the flanks, spending ammunition on the right targets and avoiding encirclement compete; spreading out to fight everywhere is the naive risk. Evasion should be harder than in the compact defender pilots, a hypothesis to verify. Screened 2026-10-15: the lobby takes both rosters at 12000 and the AI attacks.

chd-reserve-grn-siege.name: chd-reserve-grn-siege
chd-reserve-grn-siege.brief: Trade outer territory for time while committing one mobile reserve and limited construction supplies.

ksl-reserves-survival.name: ksl-reserves-survival
ksl-reserves-survival.brief: Buy immediate relief or preserve supplies for a more expensive reinforcement; sustain ammunition and fresh troops against native waves.

sla-detachments-dwf-conquest.name: sla-detachments-dwf-conquest
sla-detachments-dwf-conquest.brief: Contest the central ticket-generating point or raid supporting shooters. Reference evidence: its single point cannot test distributed objective control.

emp-battery-wef-evacuation.name: emp-battery-wef-evacuation
emp-battery-wef-evacuation.brief: Escort two batteries to a public extraction zone before a deadline while scouting concealed Wood Elf threats.

custom.rules: Escort batteries f7 and f8 to the extraction circle before 900 seconds. Both must have living crews and be inside the circle together, neither routing nor shattered. Alternatively, win the native battle with both batteries surviving before the deadline. Losing either battery or reaching the deadline without success loses the objective. A single battery in the zone is partial progress; it remains vulnerable and controllable.

emp-battery-skv-evacuation.name: emp-battery-skv-evacuation
emp-battery-skv-evacuation.brief: Escort two batteries to a public extraction zone before a deadline while scouting stalking Skaven threats.

ksl-raiders-emp-halberds.name: ksl-raiders-emp-halberds
ksl-raiders-emp-halberds.brief: Two units of Kislev Horse Raiders attack one unit of Empire Halberdiers, with no lords. Halberds resist cavalry charges from the front; the riders are three times as fast. Fixing the block with one unit while the other charges its flank or rear, then pulling out and repeating, competes with a frontal charge. Hypotheses, not a prescribed solution; winnability is not yet shown.

brt-archers-dwf-slayers.brief: Two Mounted Yeomen Archer units attack one unbreakable Slayer unit. Compared with Horse Archers, these cheaper riders have weaker missiles and melee performance. Finite ammunition and safe firing angles must support a possible melee finish.

brt-archers-dwf-slayers-decoy.name: brt-archers-dwf-slayers-decoy
brt-archers-dwf-slayers-decoy.brief: Two Mounted Yeomen Archer units attack one unbreakable Slayer unit escorted by one shielded Dwarf Warriors unit. Arrows spent on the armoured, shielded decoy are lost to the Slayers; which unit to shoot, from where, and when to finish in melee decide whether the ammunition lasts.

emp-handgunners-dwf-warriors.name: emp-handgunners-dwf-warriors
emp-handgunners-dwf-warriors.brief: One Empire Spearmen unit and two Handgunner units attack two shielded Dwarf Warrior units, with no lords. Handguns fire low and cannot shoot over friends, and dwarf shields block frontal shots; the spearmen lose a long melee. Where the guns stand once the lines meet competes with firing from behind the line. Hypotheses, not a prescribed solution; winnability is not yet shown.

emp-handgunners-dwf-warriors-3.name: emp-handgunners-dwf-warriors-3
emp-handgunners-dwf-warriors-3.brief: One Empire Spearmen unit and two Handgunner units attack three shielded Dwarf Warrior units, with no lords. The spearmen cannot hold for long, the dwarf shields block frontal shots, and low-trajectory guns cannot shoot over friends; where the guns stand and whom they shoot decide the fight.

emp-wizard-emp-swordsmen.name: emp-wizard-emp-swordsmen
emp-wizard-emp-swordsmen.brief: A Bright Wizard and one Spearmen unit attack two Empire Swordsmen units, with no lords. Fire spells can win a two-to-one infantry fight but also burn the wizard's own line, and the opening magic pool is small. When, where and on whom to spend it competes with casting at first sight. Hypotheses, not a prescribed solution; winnability is not yet shown.
emp-wizard-emp-swordsmen.calibration_change: Small focused candidate S5 (b18, 2026-10-17; calibration/micro-scenarios-draft-20261016.md). Draft database costs: player 600 (250 + 350), enemy 750. Empire mirror as in emp5-emp5. Defined only: a hero-led lordless roster, the wizard's lore and the 800 custom funds are unverified. Scripted probe_abilities and attack_nearest floors, then the disclosed SpellWindow diagnostic at 0 and 5 s observation age, before any model battle. emp-knights-emp-swordsmen.name: emp-knights-emp-swordsmen
emp-knights-emp-swordsmen.brief: One Swordsmen unit and one Empire Knights unit attack three Empire Swordsmen units, with no lords. The infantry cannot hold three units for long; the knights hit hard from behind but suffer in a prolonged melee. Pinning, rear charges, pulling out and moving on after a rout compete with a frontal charge. Hypotheses, not a prescribed solution; winnability is not yet shown.
emp-knights-emp-swordsmen.calibration_change: Small focused candidate S6 (b18, 2026-10-17; calibration/micro-scenarios-draft-20261016.md). Draft database costs: player 1225 (375 + 850), enemy 1125. emp-knights-emp-swordsmen-2.name: emp-knights-emp-swordsmen-2
emp-knights-emp-swordsmen-2.brief: One Swordsmen unit and one Empire Knights unit attack two Empire Swordsmen units, with no lords. The infantry can hold one unit for a while but not both; the knights hit hard from behind but suffer in a prolonged melee. Pinning, rear charges, pulling out and moving on after a rout compete with a frontal charge. Hypotheses, not a prescribed solution; winnability is not yet shown.

emp-pitched-grn-20.name: emp-pitched-grn-20
emp-pitched-grn-20.brief: Twenty Empire units, with a General and a Bright Wizard, attack twenty Greenskin units of equal cost on an open map with a 40-minute timer. Halberds and spears against wolves and boars, guns behind their own line, a wizard beside friendly troops and two artillery pieces to protect are the small scenarios' problems at once; the AI can also call Waaagh army abilities. The question is whether those skills survive forty units, a long history and a high order volume. Hypotheses, not a prescribed solution; winnability is not yet shown.
emp-pitched-grn-20.calibration_change: Larger candidate L1 (b19, 2026-10-17; calibration/micro-scenarios-draft-20261016.md). Draft database costs: Empire 10,375, Greenskins 10,350 (1,308 against 1,428 men), lords on, funds 10,500, 2400 s timer. Every card appears in recorded lobby dumps. Defined only: setup, battle duration, observation size and decision delay at forty units await attack_nearest and skills setup battles; a scripted win is not expected. Overlaps swarm command on order volume. Funds raised above the army costs (2026-10-17): the S5 lobby refused readiness at 800 funds (a player had spent too much on their army setup) although the database costs sum to 600/750, so a character's lobby price exceeds its database cost. Rosters are fixed; funds only cap recruitment. Was 10500. Raised again to 15000 after S5's 1200 refusal: four characters may carry lobby markups.

ksl-ffa-grn-dwf-12.name: ksl-ffa-grn-dwf-12
ksl-ffa-grn-dwf-12.brief: Twelve Kislev units in a four-way free-for-all against twelve AI Greenskin, twelve AI Dwarf and twelve AI Empire units, each army in its own alliance, with a 40-minute timer. The three AI armies also fight each other, so when to stay out, whom to engage and when to commit compete over a long horizon. Hypotheses, not a prescribed solution; winnability is not yet shown.
ksl-ffa-grn-dwf-12.calibration_change: Larger candidate L2 (b19, 2026-10-17; calibration/micro-scenarios-draft-20261016.md). The draft costs Kislev at 7,350 and asks for AI armies near 7,100 (Greenskins) and 7,450 (Dwarfs, Dwarf Warriors with great weapons instead of Ironbreakers); the two AI rosters here are b19 choices from cards in recorded lobby dumps, estimated from the siege and swarm anchors' totals, not database-checked. The four-army five-unit free-for-all was won by attack_nearest (942 s) and an LLM (560 s), so AIs fight each other. Defined only: three-army slots, the 7,500 funds readback (every roster must fit), player_defends false (the earlier free-for-all recorded the player as attacker) and the alliances await a setup battle. Fallback if the AIs both target the player: a three-point Domination. Funds raised above the army costs (2026-10-17): the S5 lobby refused readiness at 800 funds (a player had spent too much on their army setup) although the database costs sum to 600/750, so a character's lobby price exceeds its database cost. Rosters are fixed; funds only cap recruitment. Was 7500. Raised again to 11000 after S5's 1200 refusal: characters may carry lobby markups. Version 2 (2026-10-17, after queue E1): the lobby refused the three-army version (bench-b23-l2-setup-20261017: "Free-For-All requires 4 teams"), so a fourth army joins as the last AI slot: twelve Empire units, a General with a Bright Wizard, every card recruited in L1's lobby (b23). The id keeps its b19 name. Database costs (scripts/wh3_db.py, main_units_tables multiplayer_cost): Kislev 7,350 (832 men), Greenskins 6,875 (918), Dwarfs 6,875 (973), Empire 6,875 (916); the b19 AI rosters were 6,875 each, not the drafted 7,100/7,450. Funds 15000 (was 11000), as in L1: lobbies that started put the character markups at most 4,625 for L1's General with a Bright Wizard, 4,650 for its Warboss with a Shaman, 600 for a Dwarf Lord (12,000 funds, 11,400 database), so every side keeps at least 3,475 above its proven bound; Kislev's Boyar with a Frost Maiden has no bound yet and 7,650 headroom.

dwf-longbeards-emp-swordsmen.name: dwf-longbeards-emp-swordsmen
dwf-longbeards-emp-swordsmen.brief: Two Dwarf Longbeard units, with no lord, defend against four Empire Swordsmen units. The swordsmen are faster and can wrap the dwarfs' flanks and rear in the open; the observation carries the map bounds and restricted terrain cells but no elevation. Where to stand before contact competes with holding where deployed. Hypotheses, not a prescribed solution; winnability is not yet shown.
dwf-longbeards-emp-swordsmen.calibration_change: Small focused candidate S7 (b19, 2026-10-17; calibration/micro-scenarios-draft-20261016.md), the draft's lowest-confidence item. Draft database costs: player 1,400 (2 x 700), enemy 1,500 (4 x 375). Defined only: lordless setup and 1,500 funds await their live check; then a hold floor and the disclosed CornerHold diagnostic at 0 and 5 s observation age, before any model battle. Longbeards may win in the open, and a gap may remain behind a line at the map edge. Funds raised above the army costs (2026-10-17): the S5 lobby refused readiness at 800 funds (a player had spent too much on their army setup) although the database costs sum to 600/750, so a character's lobby price exceeds its database cost. Rosters are fixed; funds only cap recruitment. Was 1500.

dwf-longbeards-emp-swordsmen-6.name: dwf-longbeards-emp-swordsmen-6
dwf-longbeards-emp-swordsmen-6.brief: Two Dwarf Longbeard units defend against six Empire Swordsmen units, with no lords. Enough enemies to wrap both flanks: backing into a corner or against blocked ground limits how many can reach the Dwarfs at once.
dwf-longbeards-emp-swordsmen-6.calibration_change: S7 second step (2026-10-17). The hold floor won the four-unit version easily (bench-b20-s7-floor-20261017: 469 s, Longbeards 69 and 70 of 75, all Swordsmen routed), the draft's stated risk. Six Swordsmen (database 375 each, 2250) so an envelopment is possible; funds 2500. Hold floor first; CornerHold at 0/5 s after a floor loss.

dwf-longbeards-emp-greatswords-2.name: dwf-longbeards-emp-greatswords-2
dwf-longbeards-emp-greatswords-2.brief: Two Dwarf Longbeard units, with no lord, defend against two Empire Greatswords units and two Swordsmen units. The Greatswords' armour-piercing blades cut through the dwarf armour that turns ordinary swords, and all four units are faster and can wrap the dwarfs' flanks and rear in the open; the observation carries the map bounds and restricted terrain cells but no elevation. Where to stand before contact, and which face meets the Greatswords, compete with holding where deployed. Hypotheses, not a prescribed solution; winnability is not yet shown.
dwf-longbeards-emp-greatswords-2.calibration_change: S7 third step (2026-10-17, delegated while the owner was away). The hold floor won against four Swordsmen (bench-b20-s7-floor-20261017: 469 s, Longbeards 69 and 70 of 75) and against six (bench-b23-s7-floor-6-20261017: 612 s, Longbeards 58 and 39 of 75): numbers alone do not bind. Database stats: Swordsmen blades deal 21 base + 7 armour-piercing damage against Longbeard armour 100. From the four-unit version, two Swordsmen become Greatswords (database 850 each; 10 base + 25 armour-piercing, +14 against infantry, plate armour 95, leadership 75; custom-battle card for wh_main_emp_empire). Four attackers keep the envelopment. Enemy 2450 (2 x 850 + 2 x 375), near the six-Swordsmen step's 2250 that the floor won with the Longbeards worn down; player 1400; funds 2750. Four Greatswords (3400) are the next step if the floor wins. Hold floor first; CornerHold at 0/5 s only after a floor loss.

dwf-thunderers-grn-trolls.name: dwf-thunderers-grn-trolls
dwf-thunderers-grn-trolls.brief: Two Dwarf Thunderer units and one Dwarf Warriors unit defend against three regenerating Troll units, with no lords. Spread fire heals back; which troll unit the guns shoot, and who takes the first contact in front of them, decide whether any troll unit breaks before the clubs reach the guns.
dwf-thunderers-grn-trolls.calibration_change: Small focused candidate S8 (b20, 2026-10-17; docs/twwarhammer3/small-scenarios-2.md). Database costs: player 1850 (2 x 700 + 450), enemy 2250 (3 x 750); funds 2500 for headroom. Defined only: lordless Dwarf/Greenskin recruitment and the Trolls' regeneration in battle are unverified. Floor hold first.

dwf-thunderers-grn-trolls-2.name: dwf-thunderers-grn-trolls-2
dwf-thunderers-grn-trolls-2.brief: Two Dwarf Thunderer units and one Dwarf Warriors unit defend against two regenerating Troll units, with no lords. Spread fire heals back; which troll unit the guns shoot, and who takes the first contact in front of them, decide whether a troll unit breaks before the clubs reach the guns.
dwf-thunderers-grn-trolls-2.calibration_change: S8 step down (2026-10-17, delegated while the owner was away). Against three Trolls the hold floor lost at 136 s (bench-b20-s8-floor-20261017) and FocusFire lost both battles at 147 s and 149 s (bench-b22-s8-focus-20261017): no Troll died after 66-120 rounds per gun unit, and every Dwarf unit routed. One Troll unit fewer (database 750; enemy 1500, player 1850); funds 2500 and everything else unchanged. Hold floor first, since it may now win; FocusFire at 0/5 s only after a floor loss.

grn-giant-ksl-streltsi.name: grn-giant-ksl-streltsi
grn-giant-ksl-streltsi.brief: One Greenskin Giant attacks a Kislev Kossar spear unit and a Streltsi rifle unit, with no lords. The spears are braced against large monsters; the riflemen are not, but they shoot armour-piercing rounds as the Giant approaches. Which unit to reach first, and by what route, decides the fight.
grn-giant-ksl-streltsi.calibration_change: Small focused candidate S9 (b20, 2026-10-17; docs/twwarhammer3/small-scenarios-2.md). Database costs: player 1400, enemy 1350 (500 + 850); funds 1600. Defined only: a one-unit lordless monster army is unverified. Floor attack_nearest first.

grn-giant-ksl-streltsi-trolls.name: grn-giant-ksl-streltsi-trolls
grn-giant-ksl-streltsi-trolls.brief: A Greenskin Giant and one Troll unit attack a Kislev Kossar spear unit and a Streltsi rifle unit, with no lords. Both Greenskin units are large, and the spears are braced against large units; the riflemen are not, but they shoot armour-piercing rounds during the approach. Which unit each monster reaches first, together or apart, and by what route, decides the fight.
grn-giant-ksl-streltsi-trolls.calibration_change: S9 rebalance (2026-10-17, delegated while the owner was away). With the Giant alone (1400 against 1350) neither target order won: the attack-nearest floor broke the Kossars first, then the untouched Streltsi shot the Giant until it routed (bench-b20-s9-floor-20261017: lost at 542 s); MonsterTarget went for the Streltsi first (68 to 17 and 38 men) but the Giant routed early and the Kossars never engaged (bench-b23-s9-monster-20261017: lost at 276 s and 242 s). One enemy unit fewer would leave no target to choose, so the player gets a second, smaller monster instead: one Troll unit (database 750, the cheapest base-game Greenskin monster card; a second Giant would double the army to 2800). Both player units are large, so the Kossars' bracing still applies to each, and one can now pin the spears while the other reaches the riflemen. Player 2150, enemy 1350; funds 2400. The report label drops 'lone'; the family, its split group, stays S9's. Attack-nearest floor first; MonsterTarget (which sends every unit to the same target by the same flank route) at 0/5 s only after a floor loss.

skv-spears-sla-hellstriders.name: skv-spears-sla-hellstriders
skv-spears-sla-hellstriders.brief: Three Skaven Clanrat Spearmen units defend against two fearsome Hellstrider cavalry units that never rout, with no lords. Braced spear fronts stop charges; open flanks and rears invite them. Formation and facing decide whether the rats can wear the riders down.
skv-spears-sla-hellstriders.calibration_change: Small focused candidate S10 (b20, 2026-10-17; docs/twwarhammer3/small-scenarios-2.md). Database costs: player 975 (3 x 325), enemy 1350 (2 x 675); funds 1500. Defined only: lordless Skaven/Slaanesh recruitment is unverified. Floors hold and attack_nearest first.

skv-spears-sla-hellstriders-3.name: skv-spears-sla-hellstriders-3
skv-spears-sla-hellstriders-3.brief: Three Clanrat Spearmen units defend against three Hellstrider units, with no lords. Enough riders to charge every face of the block at once; facing, bracing and counter-charges decide whether the rats hold.
skv-spears-sla-hellstriders-3.calibration_change: S10 second step (2026-10-17). The hold floor won the two-rider version at 207 s (bench-b20-s10-floor-20261017): the AI charged braced fronts head-on, the draft's trivial risk, and both Hellstrider units routed (the draft read immune_to_psychology as never routing; live state says otherwise). One more Hellstriders unit (database 675, enemy 2025); funds 2250. Hold floor first; BraceFacing at 0/5 s after a floor loss.

dwf-cannon-grn-lobbers.name: dwf-cannon-grn-lobbers
dwf-cannon-grn-lobbers.brief: One Dwarf Cannon and one Dwarf Warriors unit attack two Goblin Rock Lobbers screened by two Goblin Spearmen units, with no lords. Marching under two lobbers' fire is costly; silencing them first takes the cannon's limited rounds and time.
dwf-cannon-grn-lobbers.calibration_change: Small focused candidate S11 (b20, 2026-10-17; docs/twwarhammer3/small-scenarios-2.md), the lowest-confidence item of the batch. Database costs: player 1250 (800 + 450), enemy 1750 (2 x 550 + 2 x 325); funds 1950. Defined only: lordless recruitment and the AI's use of defending artillery are unverified. Floor attack_nearest first.

dwf-cannon-grn-lobbers-1.name: dwf-cannon-grn-lobbers-1
dwf-cannon-grn-lobbers-1.brief: One Dwarf Cannon and one Dwarf Warriors unit attack one Goblin Rock Lobber screened by two Goblin Spearmen units, with no lords. Marching under the lobber's fire is costly; silencing it first takes the cannon's limited rounds and time, while the two large goblin blocks still outnumber the Warriors.
dwf-cannon-grn-lobbers-1.calibration_change: S11 step down (2026-10-17, delegated while the owner was away). Against two Rock Lobbers neither target order won: the attack-nearest floor routed the Goblin Spearmen but the intact lobbers broke the Warriors and the cannon crew (bench-b20-s11-floor-20261017: lost at 509 s), and CounterBattery silenced the lobbers (one routed, then both) but the lone Warriors and the cannon then lost to the two 120-man Goblin Spearmen blocks (bench-b23-s11-counter-20261017: lost at 346 s and 564 s). One Rock Lobber fewer (database 550; enemy 1200, player 1250); funds 1950 and everything else unchanged. Attack-nearest floor first, since it may now win; CounterBattery at 0/5 s only after a floor loss.
